annotationRationale: Divisibility restrictions bound the set's size when its minimum is small. Excluding all smaller minima and constructing a valid set with minimum 4 proves the extremal claim.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official solution, excluding minima 1, 2, and 3 and then verifying the official example with minimum 4.

review.mathCheck: Minimum 1 permits only one element. Minimum 2 permits at most five because 3 and 9 conflict. Minimum 3 permits at most five because the disjoint pairs {4,8} and {5,10} each lose an element. The displayed valid six-element set attains minimum 4, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of the first MAA Q17 solution on page 7. It expands the disjoint-pair argument and explicitly verifies the official construction.
review.annotationCheck: All smaller possible minima are excluded, and attainment is checked. No appeal to the alternative chain argument or advanced theorem is needed.
